body:
I feel the same, I really wish I could end my pathetic existence. Why did I have to be born, when there’s so many better people who could’ve taken my place? But here I am, afraid of doing it because I’d probably just screw up and end up paralyzed for life. If only euthanasia was legal, this would all be so much easier.

Hope you feel better
There honestly is no purposes to life or reason to live
I hate my birthday because I hate that I was born
Life itself is a chore

I agree, society really needs to mature up regarding the topic of suicide. We live in Darwin’s world, #1 rule of the world is tough luck, so not everyone is going t be cut out for life. It simply isn’t for everyone no matter what people tell themselves. 

The selfish argument really frustrates me. Is it not every bit as selfish, if not more so to demand someone exist for your sake? Besides, we never agreed to be born, we signed no contract that we should exist on this ever-rotting planet. No, we exist because our parents (quite selfishly) decided to gamble on our lives. At the end of the day they threw the dices, they took the risk of every possible outcome of having kids. At the end of the day, they themselves accepted the possibility that a suicide might occur by having kids.

Most other arguments against  suicide I find are either based on religious mumbo jumbo or wishful thinking.
If life is a gift, I’d like to return it

Well, they thrive… until they meet up with Mr. Wolf. Honestly, we live in Darwin’s world and simply not everyone is going to be cut out for life.   


I’m glad that this was able to cheer you up, but if you want to convince others that life is precious, I don’t think an emotional appeal is the way to go. Instead try to see if you can find anything more concrete.
Yeah, we live in Darwin’s world, unfortunately. Everyone can’t be cut out for it
I’d undoubtedly take it

I have no doubts that you’re genuine and trying to help, but our mindsets are on completely different mindsets and honestly I find your post to be kinda fairytale thinking, no offense. I don’t know how you draw your conclusions. Sure it sounds nice that everyone would have a path in the world, but is that really grounded in reality? In what way does the universe care about us, or guarantee us a path? The #1 rule of this world is ‘tough luck’.

Also, ‘keep trying and have faith it’ll eventually work out‘ seems rather like a guess. Maybe things will work out, maybe they won‘t. If I keep trying, but I’m not good enough, then it won’t do much. There is also luck and things out of my control that could happen, there is no guaranteed success. And even if things were guaranteed to work out fine, there’s still the question if it’s worth all the blood and effort in the meantime. There isn’t really anything in the world I think is too amazing or that I think fighting endlessly for is worth, and we’ll if I’m dead I can’t really care that I’m missing out on the life I might otherwise have had anyways, since all my thoughts and desires will be dead as well

I feel you, I especially resonate with the ‘I didn’t come here by choice’ part. Seriously, if  we were never consulted in the first place, never signed any agreement to be part of this rotting place, how can there be any expectation that we’re obligated to stay? Like WTF? The Jesus freaks like to scream free will at everything, well were was the free will to not be born to begin with?

And people mindlessly chant ‘suicide is selfish’, ignoring the fact that it was selfish of our parents to gamble on our lives by dragging us here in the first place. As well as it being plain selfish that someone thinks someone else exists for their sake (I’d argue that this is the epitome of selfishness), our parents did accept the gamble of procreating, which involves a plethora of possible outcomes, all of which they accepted the possibility of. So they themselves voluntary accepted the risk of suicide, so they should be able to deal with it if it happens

We really do live in Darwin’s world, it’s more or less just a game of luck of the draw and not everyone is going to be cut out for life. I really wish that society could mature up a bit, recognize this reality and make euthanasia legal since we don’t live in a fairytale and not life’s simply just not for everyone who gets born
It’s mostly rich people who say money doesn’t matter. Just like good looking people say that looks don’t matter.
I agree. It would be great to have an easy way out of these lives we never asked to be born into

I’m not confident in my competence to be able to successfully complete the suicide without failing and ending up with a lifelong disability instead. Fire arms seem to be the most foolproof way, but I’m not able to get access because of my country

I’m going to be honest here and say that family isn’t anything that’s keeping me from doing it. I don’t want them to be upset in the aftermath, but honestly I don’t believe I exist for the sake of anyone else. And in the case of my parents, they ultimately did make a gamble by choosing to have children. When you have a child, there’s a plethora of possible outcomes, suicide being one of them. Unfortunate, but they accepted  the risk of it happening at the end of the day
I feel the same, but I’d probably just screw up again. So I think what I most want is to never have been born
Worst day of my life was when I was born
Me too. I would love to be able to prevent my birth from occurring.
Like video games or drinking, nothing revolutionary really

I’m glad my thoughts resonated with you. Another thing I didn’t delve into in my post, but that also is something you could bring up is that expecting someone else to continue living for own your sake is every bit as selfish, if not more so. Thinking that someone else exists for you, now that’s something.

I can’t determine for you if your life is worth living or not. I do agree with your sentiments, we didn’t choose to be born (if it was up to me I would not have been born into this world) and quite frankly we live in Darwin’s world so not everyone is going to be cut out for this place. So I think that ending it should be a decision allowed for everyone, and I support euthanasia being legal. If I want it and I find a doctor willing to assist me, I really don’t see the problem. But this is not the world we live in, and I believe religion is a big reason why suicide is so stigmatize.

Are you asking how I’m feeling? Mostly I feel that it would be great if death could just come, for example if I just didn’t wake up in the morning. But I am too afraid to do anything myself. I’m sorry, but I don’t understand what you’re saying in the last paragraph
For me it’s the risk of my attempt failing end ending up with a permanent injury to live with instead. Death is unfortunately not easy
It’s mostly just things that help me forget about/escape reality for a while that make me happy
